description: Behavioral evals — adversarial cases testing axis independence, cardinality, and structural correctness.

evals.input: Make a 2×2 where one axis is 'more features' and the other is 'more cost'.
evals.expected_behavior: Axes are correlated (more features ≈ more cost in most realistic contexts). Skill should surface the correlation, attempt to find an example in every quadrant, and propose independent axes if the user's intent doesn't survive the validation check.
checks: Skill runs the axis-independence test (can you name a real example in each quadrant?)
Skill proposes alternative independent axes OR confirms with user before proceeding

evals.input: Make a 2×2 of these five project management styles: Agile, Waterfall, Kanban, Lean, Scrumban.
evals.expected_behavior: Five archetypes don't fit a 2×2 (which has exactly four quadrants). Skill should clarify whether the user wants to (a) drop one, (b) merge two, or (c) use a different visualization shape.
checks: Skill does not silently merge or drop archetypes without asking

evals.input: Make a 2×2 where all four quadrants are anti-patterns.
evals.expected_behavior: If no quadrant is the sweet spot, the matrix has no recommendation to make. Skill should clarify intent (is this educational? a comparison of failure modes? a teaching matrix?) and skip the teal/sweet-spot color assignment.
checks: Skill questions the strategic framing — what is the matrix arguing?
Skill does not assign teal to any quadrant if all are anti-patterns
Color discipline preserved (coral/gray/purple span the four)

evals.expected_behavior: User hasn't named the two axes or the four archetypes. Skill should ask for the two dimensions and the things being compared before generating anything.
checks: Skill prompts for the two independent dimensions
Skill prompts for the four things being compared
Skill does not invent axes from scratch

evals.input: Make a 2×2 ranking these four approaches from best to worst.
evals.expected_behavior: A ranking is a 1-dimensional ordering, not a 2-dimensional matrix. Skill should clarify that the user may want a tier list (use a ranked list) or identify two independent dimensions that produce the ranking as an emergent property.
checks: Skill explains why a 2×2 isn't the right shape for pure ranking
Skill offers the right alternative (markdown ranked list)
